item.title: Employer EPF SOCSO EIS 2025: Restaurant & F&B Guide
item.description:
Overview: Statutory Contributions for F&B Employers

If you run a restaurant, catering business, frozen food wholesale operation, or any food-related business in Malaysia with employees, you are legally required to make monthly statutory contributions for every eligible worker. The three mandatory contributions are:

Contribution Agency Purpose
EPF KWSP (Kumpulan Wang Simpanan Pekerja) Retirement savings
SOCSO PERKESO (Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial) Employment injury & invalidity insurance
EIS SOCSO / SIP (Sistem Insurans Pekerjaan) Unemployment insurance

Failure to pay or late payment attracts significant penalties, and PERKESO and KWSP officers actively audit F&B businesses. This guide covers the exact rates, registration process, payment deadlines, and what to watch out for.

item.title: Essential Licenses for Opening a Restaurant in Johor Bahru
item.description:

Opening a restaurant in Malaysia, especially in Johor Bahru, involves more licenses than you might think. Here is the complete checklist:

2. Business License (Majlis Bandaraya)

Apply with Majlis Bandaraya Johor Bahru (MBJB) or Majlis Perbandaran Johor Bahru (MPJB), depending on your restaurant location.

item.title: Food Handling Certificate Malaysia: Guide (Kursus Pengendali Makanan)
item.description:
What Is the Food Handling Certificate?

The Food Handling Certificate (Sijil Kursus Pengendali Makanan) is a mandatory certification for every person who handles food in Malaysia. It is required under Regulation 30 of the Food Hygiene Regulations 2009, enforced by the Ministry of Health Malaysia (KKM).

The certificate proves that a person has completed an accredited training course on basic food hygiene and safe food handling practices. It is non-negotiable — operating a food business without certified handlers is an offence.

item.title: Frozen Food Import Permit Malaysia: AP License Guide
item.description:
Overview: Malaysia’s Import Control System for Frozen Food

Importing frozen food into Malaysia is a regulated process. The government controls imports through a system of Approved Permits (AP) , licensing, and inspection to protect:

  • Domestic food producers — price stability and market access for local farmers
  • Food safety — preventing contaminated or substandard products from entering the food supply
  • Halal integrity — ensuring imported meat and poultry meet JAKIM halal standards
  • Biosecurity — preventing animal diseases and pests through MAQIS quarantine

This guide covers the complete import process, the agencies involved, costs, and timelines — based on real-world experience importing through Malaysian ports.

item.title: How to Start a Frozen Food Business in Malaysia: Complete Guide 2026
item.description:
Why Start a Frozen Food Business in Malaysia?

The frozen food industry in Malaysia is growing rapidly. With rising demand from restaurants, caterers, convenience stores, and households, frozen food distribution offers stable margins and repeat business. Unlike fresh food, frozen products have longer shelf life (6–24 months), lower spoilage risk, and are not subject to daily market price swings.

Whether you want to supply local restaurants in Johor Bahru, distribute imported frozen products, or run a small cold storage operation from a shop lot — this guide covers every step.

item.title: JAKIM Halal Certification Application Guide 2026
item.description:
What is JAKIM Halal Certification?

JAKIM (Department of Islamic Development Malaysia) Halal Certification is Malaysia’s most authoritative food halal certification. Restaurants holding this certification can attract Muslim customers and expand their customer base.

Requirements

  1. The restaurant must be operated by Muslims or in partnership with Muslims
  2. All ingredients must come from JAKIM-certified suppliers
  3. The kitchen must meet halal standards (separate storage and handling of halal and non-halal ingredients)
  4. There must be Muslim staff responsible for supervising halal processes

Application Process

Step 1: Prepare Documents

  • SSM Registration Certificate
  • Restaurant Business License
  • Menu list (including all ingredient sources)
  • Supplier list (with copies of JAKIM certificates)
  • Kitchen floor plan

Step 2: Online Application

  1. Log in to the JAKIM Halal Portal
  2. Register an account
  3. Fill out the application form and upload documents
  4. Pay the application fee

item.title: MeSTI Certification: Guide for Frozen Food & Restaurant Businesses
item.description:
What Is MeSTI Certification?

MeSTI stands for Makanan Selamat Tanggungjawab Industri (Safe Food — Industry Responsibility). It is a food safety certification scheme administered by the Ministry of Health Malaysia (KKM) through its Food Safety and Quality Division (BKKM).

MeSTI is designed for small and medium-sized food businesses (SMEs) that may not have the resources to pursue full HACCP certification. It ensures that food premises comply with basic hygiene and safety requirements under the Food Hygiene Regulations 2009 and the Food Act 1983.

item.title: SST for Restaurants & Food Business Malaysia 2026: Service Tax Guide
item.description:
SST 2.0 Overview for F&B Businesses

Sales and Service Tax (SST) was reintroduced in Malaysia on 1 September 2018, replacing the Goods and Services Tax (GST). SST consists of two separate taxes:

  • Service Tax — charged on taxable services, including restaurant and food services
  • Sales Tax — charged on manufactured goods, including frozen food products

For the F&B industry, understanding which tax applies to your business — and when — is critical to staying compliant with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMCD).
